result.title: Does Pretraining Teach Chemical Language Models Chemistry?
result.summary: Chemical language models (CLMs) are pretrained on large corpora of molecules with the aim of learning representations that transfer to diverse downstream tasks. Here, we systematically study the effects of pretraining using a series of such CLMs across 64 molecular property prediction datasets. We find that the downstream gains of pretraining in CLMs do not scale and performance saturates below gradient-boosting baselines. Across the regimes evaluated, only supervised pretraining on traditional physico-chemical descriptors consistently improves downstream performance for the CLMs tested whereas some forms of pretraining result in models worse than a randomly initialized encoder. While models can resolve molecular structure well, they do so no better than a randomly initialized model, suggesting that, at best, CLMs learn descriptor-like properties in addition to low-level token statistics during pretraining, but surprisingly little chemistry beyond what classical molecular features already capture.

AI.brief_summary: 在 64 个分子性质预测数据集上系统检验化学语言模型预训练的收益：下游提升不随预训练规模扩展、性能饱和且低于梯度提升基线，仅基于传统理化描述符的监督预训练带来稳定改善，模型解析分子结构的能力也不优于随机初始化编码器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预训练模型 vs 随机初始化编码器 + 经典特征基线」的受控诊断范式，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真编码视觉证据而非仅保留低层 token 统计，属方法线索而非直接主线研究。
